newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria reports truce violations in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria reports truce violations in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Nigeria said on Thursday that forces loyal to Sierra Leone's coup leaders were breaking a ceasefire with West African ECOMOG troops massed there to restore constitutional rule.

"The coupists and their rebel allies have continued to conduct probing attacks on ECOMOG troop locations in Kossoh, Jiu, Hastings airfield, Lungi airport and its environs presumably in search of the FM radio station believed to be harboured by ECOMOG," Nigeria's defence headquarters spokesman said in a statement in Lagos.

The West African force met representatives of the junta in Ivory Coast last week and announced an immediate halt to fighting that has broken out intermittently since the May 25 coup that toppled elected president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Kabbah, who fled to neighbouring Guinea, made a clandestine broadcast into Sierra Leone two weeks ago on a radio station the coup leaders said was set up the Nigerian-dominated ECOMOG.
The Nigerian spokesman said that in the past two days some civilians, military and paramilitary personnel loyal to Kabbah had surrendered to ECOMOG.
"The villages of such people have been attacked and burnt," he said, adding that the latest such attacks took place at Bo and Kanema towns on Thursday morning.
The two sides are due to meet again in Abidjan soon to try to resolve the standoff that has persisted since the coup.
The Nigerian statement said :"The ECOMOG troops have been provoked beyond limits and will not hesitate to be on counter offensive for self-defence."
Despite the incessant armed clashes between both sides a widely expected all out attack by Nigeria to reverse the Sierra Leone coup never materialised.
